hypothesis: Can a tiny native 3-param Torch-trained future-relevance scorer govern eviction in the original 576-byte, 7-active/9-retained StatePool, preserving unfamiliar four-hop relational knowledge under 12-edge overload better than FIFO and LRU?
architecture: Unchanged Y-NCI02 native Torch admission (4 weights), native learned join (6 weights), and NCI05 multiedge StatePool. New Torch nn.Linear(2,1) admission to retention, learned from development-only public exposure/time features and labels of future relevance. No future labels given at sealed inference. Sequential StatePool evictions and checkpoint restoration use original state_dict.
task: 96 sealed cases, 24 seeds × 4 motifs, 12 observed relationships in original random-free structural streams. Seven active edges max per arm; public rehearsal at observation 6 only; answer two-hop, four-hop and after checkpoint, versus original native learned join and full graph oracle. Three policies same stream but distinct capacity-limited states.
registered_verdict: LEARNED_BOUNDED_RETENTION_TRANSFER iff learned four-hop >=60%, >=+15pp vs FIFO and +10pp vs LRU with no family worse than LRU by >20pp. PARTIAL_RETENTION_GAIN_WITH_GENERALIZATION_COST if >=+10pp vs FIFO only; otherwise NO_TRANSFERABLE_LEARNED_RETENTION_GAIN. No learned graph search, learned relational storage, general-purpose language or RSI claim.
guardrails: Frozen first-use identity and disjoint from Y-NCI05 sealed seeds
Only training source uses future relevance labels
Same retained-edge count for FIFO, LRU and learned
Original artifact uploaded before analysis, final full pytest and separate independent no-replay audit
Report accuracy for all families, negative and retention costs, score multiplies, join evaluator work
No FORGE R32/R33, accepted refs, CKB/KTRADE, controller, production, merge or live brokerage
